title: Retire the caller safeBoundaryObserved relay in the release carrier (derive from the durable observation)
description:

But recordAttemptRelease (attempt-release-disposition.ts) still RELAYS the caller's safeBoundaryObserved as authority, and its suite deliberately PINS that relay: :337/:566 refuse an OMITTED flag among three, :596 drives the DRAINING arm via drained("safeBoundaryObserved"), :814/:868 pass false deliberately. Deriving the field makes "refuses an OMITTED boundary flag" unreachable by construction — a contract change to 740924b7's surface.

THE SEAM: recordAttemptRelease itself — its :70 comment names ded026d6 as the awaited producer; it already receives the store and bound attempt. foundation-attempt-service.ts needs NO edit (verified — avoids the task-1879166d collision).

RULING CONSTRAINTS (from the ded026d6 record): option (c) — keep relaying and record alongside — is REJECTED: it leaves the caller's flag as authority while the row looks produced. Rail 1's intent (no agent declares its own boundary safe) is the acceptance bar for this row.

(1) PRODUCER surface CONFIRMED, but the plan's assumed entry point does NOT exist. safe-boundary-observation.ts (254 lines) exports recordSafeBoundaryObservation(:160) and readSafeBoundaryObservation(:231). readSafeBoundaryObservation takes {observationRef, projectId} — and observationRef is a sha256 over (projectId, attemptRef, JSON(providerRunRef), recordDigest) under a private REF_DOMAIN. The carrier CANNOT compute it without reimplementing digestOf/REF_DOMAIN — which would be exactly the "second boundary opinion" the plan's adversarial checklist forbids. There is NO by-attempt read exported (grep: only the two functions above). CONSEQUENCE: the only composition through the producer's real surface is recordSafeBoundaryObservation(store, {attemptRef, correlationId, key, projectId, requestBytes}) — identity + decision metadata only, every boundary fact derived inside from readCurrentProviderRun. It is replay-idempotent (expectedVersion 0 on a ref-derived aggregate), so calling it on the release path yields COMMITTED once and REPLAYED after. Its "durable-record-absent" arm is SAFE_BOUNDARY_RUN_UNREADABLE at layer DAEMON_SAFE_BOUNDARY_OBSERVATION, which is exactly step-2(c)'s pinned code.

(2) RELAY confirmed: AttemptReleaseRequest.safeBoundaryObserved: unknown (:85), kernelRequest passes it verbatim (:94), header :67-77 documents the relay.

(1) ADMISSION. carriesBoundaryClaim uses Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty, deliberately: `{safeBoundaryObserved: undefined}` is a caller that spoke about the boundary and must hear the same refusal as one that claimed true, and hasOwnProperty (not `in`/Reflect.has) keeps a hostile prototype from answering. It runs as the FIRST statement of recordAttemptRelease, before durableActivation, so a spoof cannot even cause an observation to be written on its way to being discarded — which is what the (d) case's `boundaryObservations(fixture)` toEqual([]) assertion pins.

(2) DERIVATION. deriveSafeBoundary composes recordSafeBoundaryObservation, NOT readSafeBoundaryObservation — recorded in the module header with the reason: the reader is keyed by an observationRef the producer digests under a domain it does not export, so a carrier computing that ref would reimplement the producer in order to ask the producer a question. The writer takes identity plus decision metadata only, derives every boundary fact itself and is replay-idempotent on a ref-derived aggregate. Decision metadata is composed from the bound attempt and durable activation, with commandId/correlationId suffixed ":SAFE_BOUNDARY" so the observation cannot collide with the ":RELEASED" decision the same command lands. NOTHING in the carrier re-checks an exit fact.

(3) VOCABULARY. ATTEMPT_RELEASE_CODES gained exactly one member, ATTEMPT_RELEASE_REQUEST_MALFORMED (7->8), because the admission is this daemon's own decision. AttemptReleaseLayer gained a FOURTH member, the producer's own SafeBoundaryObservationLayer, and AttemptReleaseRefused.code widened by SafeBoundaryRefusalCode — so a refusal is carried, never restamped. carryBoundaryRefusal puts the producer's upstreamCode in `message`, which is how PROVIDER_RUN_EVIDENCE_ABSENT survives two hops to reach the (c) assertion.

(4) CALL SITE. foundation-attempt-service.ts noteRelease drops the key from its literal; nothing else in that file moved, and its comment now says why (the flag is no longer ours to report). No third call site exists.

FIXTURE CORRECTION FORCED BY THE COMPOSITION, and it is a strengthening. plantedSlot hand-composed its activation decision with commandKind EFFECT_ACTIVATE_COMMAND_KIND. readFoundationActivationHistory never looks at the decision trace, so that passed — but the strict BY-ATTEMPT reader the producer binds through checks it at activation-attempt-reader.ts:151 and answered FOUNDATION_BINDING_ACTIVATION_INCOHERENT, breaking all 8 slot-family cases. Fixed by planting through the PRODUCTION writer commitActivationLedgerRecord, which stamps activation.commit and copies the event id from the grant. The plant is now more faithful to the production path than it was, and the slot drift is still judged by the production codec.
